final_answer:
Using the rice mitigator challenge data, I defined baseline insulin resistance from SSPG in `data_meta.csv` (insulin resistant if SSPG >= 150 mg/dL; insulin sensitive otherwise), computed each replicate’s peak glucose rise as post-challenge peak glucose minus mean pre-challenge baseline glucose, and fit the interaction model `peak_rise ~ insulin_resistance_status * mitigator` on the protein- and fiber-preloaded rice experiments.

The interaction effect was small and imprecise: the replicate-level interaction coefficient for insulin-resistance status × protein preload was -24.80 mg/dL (95% CI -69.77 to 20.16, p = 0.2745), with partial eta-squared = 0.0189.

Expressed as the paired protein-versus-fiber reduction metric (`fiber peak rise - protein peak rise`), protein preload reduced the rice peak by a mean of 6.94 mg/dL more than fiber in insulin-sensitive participants (n = 15), but by -15.17 mg/dL in insulin-resistant participants (n = 4), meaning protein performed worse than fiber in that small IR subgroup. The between-status difference in this paired reduction effect was 22.11 mg/dL.

Overall, baseline insulin resistance status showed only a small interaction effect on the protein-vs-fiber difference in rice peak glucose reduction in this dataset, and the estimate was not statistically precise because the SSPG-defined insulin-resistant subgroup was very small.
